column1: # Partial key of the Sormano cipher, BnF fr. 3096 (Ferrara, 1529)
# Glyphs are described in words: the shapes have no stable Unicode equivalents.
# Evidence: "L1" = line 1 of the four-line cipher on f. 124r, read glyph by glyph from crops/z128_L1exact.jpg
#   against the contemporary marginal decipherment, which gives "un capitaneo sui" for those 13 glyphs.
#   "L2" = line 2 of the same run, giving "...eri nominato" (crops/z128_L2start.jpg, z128_L2b1.jpg).
#   "g62" = the interlinear decipherment on f. 113r, which spells the same word "capitaneo".
# Confidence: firm = same value in two independent lines or letters; good = one clean occurrence.
# Homophones: a = V and round-u; i = rho, 4-with-tail, b-with-descender, psi; o = stroke and L+I; e = 4-hooked and 7.
#   Three or four alternatives for each common vowel, one or two for consonants.

column4: heads the cipher on f. 124r and the margin note that deciphers it: a tie mark, not a letter
ends cipher runs in nos. 65, 66, 67: a stop or section mark
f. 116v interlinear gloss: the cipher had a nomenclator
